proposition: During the exile Ibn Turka wrote four letters to Kārkiyā sayyids of Gilan (29 to Sayyid Aḥmad at Ranikuh, 30-31 to Sayyid Nāṣir at Lahijan, 32 to either): each in MK's description congratulates the amir on a conquest and praises his patronage of scholars or the Sufis' spiritual support, and where he declines to attend in person he cites family duties, ill health or infirmity; MK's descriptions record no request for money or protection.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Kārkiyā sayyids of Gilan
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: The silence about requests is in MK's summaries, not necessarily in the letters
